US to the Mississippi, Quebec and Rupert's Land fine; grey gap in north-eastern Minnesota (399 Quebec cells released to nobody), grey holes in Kentucky, Georgia and western Wisconsin inside the US.
Marathas with constituents, Mysore, Hyderabad, Awadh, Gwalior, Sikhs look right; the Mughal Empire has vanished from Delhi (Gwalior took its last cell on 2 Oct 1788).
Looks right: Holy Roman Empire constituents, Habsburg occupation of Wallachia hatched, Russo-Turkish contest near Ochakov, Poland and Prussia fine.
Mamluk beys in Upper Egypt and Ottoman Delta as the dossier intends; Matruh interior unowned follows Cliopatria's own Ottoman shape; Diriyah wide as Cliopatria draws it.

issues.what: Northern Iran unowned for years: the Zand ledger takes Qumis/Semnan (1781), Gilan, Qazvin, Zanjan (1782), Tehran, Hamadan, Isfahan, Qom, Kurdistan, Astarabad (1785) to the Qajar, but the Qajar dossier starts in 1789, so 635 cells of the 1668-cell north-Iran block are nobody's in 1782-84 and 1663 in 1785-88; the Qajar keyframe then takes 1830 cells at once in 1789.

Zand 1780 keyframe (Cliopatria's Karim Khan polygon) puts Mazandaran's 83 cells back for 1780-1787 although Agha Mohammad Khan conquered Mazandaran on 2 April 1779 and the Zand ledger already removes it; Mazandaran removed from that keyframe (stays unowned until the 1789 Qajar founding).

Zand ledger/14 (c. 1780: Lorestan, Ilam, Khuzestan lost) is cancelled by the same 1780 keyframe snap (Khuzestan 255 and Lorestan 121 cells stay Zand to 1787, then go to nobody in 1788 and to the Qajar in 1789 via qajar-dynasty_1788); the Agha Mohammad Khan page does not mention Kermanshah, Khuzestan or Lorestan.

United States 1783 and 1788 keyframe corrections list states inside a 92W-66W, 31N-50N box and omit Minnesota: the 399 Minnesota cells Quebec held went to nobody in 1783 and to the Spanish Empire's Louisiana region in 1788 (keyframe snap removed 489 cells in 1783); the box also cut 43 western Wisconsin and 33 southern Georgia cells and Kentucky had 31 holes. Treaty of Paris Article 2: line from the Lake of the Woods 'due west to the river Mississippi', then down the middle of the river. Both keyframes extended with Minnesota (Quebec's own polygon), Wisconsin, Kentucky and Georgia whole; the 1783 snap now removes 17 cells, not 489.

Mughal Empire disappears in October 1788: Gwalior's ledger/4 gains the whole Delhi-Agra region from it, including its one remaining cell, although Shah Alam II's second reign began on 16 October 1788 (to 1806) and he stayed emperor in Delhi as Gwalior's client. Delhi city to Palam returned to the Mughal Empire; the 1784 vassal relation to Gwalior then tints it.

Province of Quebec's own land (St Lawrence valley, Ontario, Labrador) owned by the umbrella British Colonial Empire by the colony size rule: 466 cells in 1780, 490 in 1783 (Quebec was its own colony 1763-1791); same problem the previous window ruled for 1775-1779.

Quebec's 1783 shape overlaps Rupert's Land by 266 cells of north-western Ontario (49-50N, Hudson Bay drainage); the Quebec Act set Quebec's northern limit at the southern boundary of Rupert's Land, so Rupert's Land keeps them (the size rule had given them to Quebec).
One stray cell of the East India Company (british-empire) sits in the Minnesota Arrowhead from 1788 (the dossier already removes the 30 Canadian strays of that Cliopatria shape); removed.

Mekong delta (Gia Dinh) unowned from 7 Sept 1788: Tay Son ledger/19 gives it to nguyen-dynasty, which exists only from 1802; Nguyen Anh proclaimed himself Nguyen vuong in 1780 and held the south 1788-1802, but no dossier covers his regime (nguyen-lords ends 1777).

Belize logwood zone: captaincy-general-of-guatemala ledger/5 (occupation_start, counterpart british-colonial-empire, 1783/11) has the roles reversed against the schema (the draft hatches 41 Belize cells as British land occupied by Guatemala, while the note says British cutters worked under Spanish sovereignty).
Matruh interior (365 cells) unowned from 1788: Cliopatria's Ottoman 1788 shape (verdict ok) leaves out the far Western Desert, so the 1786-87 Ottoman hold lapses.
Emirate of Diriyah 1788 shape adds 619 cells (Ha'il 288, Riyadh 205, Qassim 90) at once; dossier accepts Cliopatria's shape (verdict ok) and no page I opened dates the Najd growth.

Largest size-rule conflicts (Hyderabad/Mysore 348, Tripura/British 136, Hyderabad/Maratha 108, Awadh, Bhutan, Koch Bihar): the smaller state won each; the Mysore keyframes cite the Hyder Ali page (205,000 km2 in 1779) and the others follow the dossiers. No page opened for these.

Skipped events with unresolved names: Keta, Cormantin, Apam (Ghana) for the Danish and Dutch Gold Coast forts (about 10 cells, 1782-1787, also two Danish keyframes) and Karangan (Indonesia) for Mempawah's 1787 contest; fix needs gazetteer names, not a patch.

Other big snaps are explained by their dossiers and look right in the images: Guatemala 1788 (Petén to the captaincy, Mosquito Coast taken up after the 1786 convention), Gwalior 1788 (Delhi-Agra block), Nepal 1788, Funj/Darfur Kordofan 1782/1785, Crimea annexed April 1783 (Kuban to Russia), Mamluk beys 1786 (Upper Egypt).

dossier_requests.what: Give the Qajar polity of Agha Mohammad Khan an earlier life (or add a pre-1789 Qajar state) so the land he held is not unowned: Mazandaran from 2 April 1779, Qumis/Semnan about 1781-82, Gilan and Qazvin/Zanjan about 1782-83, Isfahan from 2 May 1785, Tehran (submitted autumn 1785, capital from 12 March 1786), Hamadan 1785.
dossier_requests.why: The Zand ledger already hands this land to the Qajar, but the dossier starts in 1789 (infobox 'Establishment: 1789'), so northern Iran is nobody's from 1782 to 1788 (up to 1663 cells). The page: 'he saw himself as the king of Iran' around 1785-86, yet 'Thus 1789 is marked as the start of his reign'. A patch cannot create a state.

dossier_requests.what: A dossier (or an extension of nguyen-lords, which ends 1777) for Nguyen Anh's regime in Gia Dinh: Nguyen vuong from 1780, holding Saigon and the Mekong delta 1778-1782 and from 7 September 1788 to 1802 (exile in Siam 1785-1787).
dossier_requests.why: The Tay Son ledger gives Gia Dinh to nguyen-dynasty in 1788, which exists only from 1802, so the delta is unowned 1788-1801 (and the contests of 1778-1785 have no live opponent).

dossier_requests.what: ledger/5 (1783/11 occupation_start, counterpart british-colonial-empire, the Belize logwood zone) has the roles reversed: the schema says the dossier's state occupies the counterpart's land, but the note describes British cutters on Spanish land. Reverse it, or move it to british-honduras.
dossier_requests.why: The draft shows 41 Belize cells as British land hatched in Guatemala's colour from 1783 on. The ledger's own source (British Honduras page) was not opened in this run.

problems: The united-states-of-america 1791 and later shapes probably carry the same omission as the 1783 and 1788 corrections (Minnesota east of the Mississippi, western Wisconsin, Kentucky holes, southern Georgia strip); not checked beyond 1790, for the p1790-p1799 agent.

keyframe_overrides/1 (united-states-of-america_1788) and keyframe_overrides/3 (british-empire_1788) run 1788-1790, so they act in 1790, the next window's first year; british-empire_1791 and _1792 may keep the same Minnesota stray cell (their corrections remove Canada only).

The trial stage differs from the published draft of 1 Nov because other windows' patches and dossier edits have landed since (e.g. Rupert's Land/Quebec/Spanish rulings of p1770-p1779); effects quoted in the patch notes are measured against a second trial of my own with an empty patch (stage0).

Contest label: 'contest spanish-florida / united-states-of-america (First Seminole War)', 151 cells since 1783, is the 31N-32N28' border dispute that began in 1783; the war name 'First Seminole War' (1817-1818) looks wrong for it (dossier united-states-of-america ledger/14); not checked against a page.

Unresolved gazetteer names (Keta, Cormantin, Apam in Ghana; Karangan in Indonesia) leave 4 skipped events and 3 unresolved keyframes (Danish Gold Coast 1784 and 1787); adding the names to the gazetteer would restore them.

United-states rulings: after the override the US holds 111 Minnesota cells (Arrowhead and east bank), Rupert's Land 202 (north-west, colony rule R1) and Spanish Louisiana 87 (west of the river, previous window's ruling); the 112 Spanish Empire cells in far northern Minnesota that the Spanish 'Louisiana' region claims were not touched.
